newsitem.title: USA: Alaska Gov. plans oil meetings in Calif., Britain.
newsitem.headline: Alaska Gov. plans oil meetings in Calif., Britain.

text.p: Alaska Gov. Tony Knowles said on Friday he will meet with oil industry officials in California and Britain in December to discuss new North Slope investments and jobs.
Knowles will meet with ARCO officials in Santa Barbara, California on December 2 and travel to London on December 8 to talk with officials of British Petroleum Co Plc .
Similar meetings are planned in Texas in early January with officials of Exxon Corp, Anadarko Petroleum Corp and United Texas Petroleum, aides to the governor said.
Knowles also will meet with Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt on December 3 in Seattle to discuss opening the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge and National Petroleum Reserve-Alaska.
The talks come in the wake of the October discovery of a 300 million barrel oil field on the Colville River, bordering on the reserve.

"With the recent announcements about the Northstar and Alpine fields, the oil industry has gotten the message that Alaska is open and ready for business," Knowles said. "This is a good time to meet with the industry to thank them for their support and foster even further investment and job growth in Alaska," he added.
